target_customer: Software engineering teams that use coding agents and need to review AI-generated code and agent traces
problem: Coding agents produce large diffs that humans struggle to review and trust. Engineers need visual, architecture-level ways to critique code, diffs and agent trajectories.
business_model: Open-source desktop apps (Whiteboard, Review) with a hosted version listed as coming soon; monetization not stated
product_category: Developer tools, AI code review and software design canvas

founders.name: Sid Menon
founders.background_notes: Led a tech team on Palantir cloud infrastructure per the YC page.

founders.name: Ketan Agrawal
education: Stanford, Symbolic Systems and computer science
founders.background_notes: Red-teamed AI systems at Robust Intelligence and built data-querying agents at Snowflake per the YC page.

competitors.name: CodeRabbit
competitors.what: AI pull request reviewer with a CLI for coding agents
competitors.funding_then: Series B announced September 2025 per a roundup

competitors.name: Greptile
competitors.traction_then: published its own 2025 benchmark claiming an 82 percent bug catch rate (vendor claim)

competitors.name: Graphite
competitors.what: Stacked pull request workflow plus AI review

technical_complexity.rationale: A cross-platform desktop app with AST-based semantic diffs (a Rust library called diffr), sequence and database diagrams and agent trace views. Standard engineering with some hard parts, built by four people.

defensibility.rationale: The apps are MIT-licensed open source, so code is freely copyable. Review tools from well-funded AI code review vendors already existed. Differentiation rests on interface design and community.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Well-funded code review vendors and coding agent makers were already shipping review features when the company launched in early 2026.

market_need_then: AI coding agents increased the volume of code needing review in 2025, and AI code review was a crowded, funded category, which shows both demand and competition.

branding.domain_note: Uses dev.fast, a country-code style domain hack; the company page links install.dev.fast.

identity.logo: Not described by any source found
identity.visual_style: Unix style naming with man-page style headings on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-native, technical, speaks in terms of confidence in your code

branding.brand_signature: Unix device path name /dev/fast and the Cursor for code review positioning
branding.community_and_virality: Whiteboard reportedly reached about 2.8K GitHub stars and has a Discord community; coverage came mostly from aggregators and blogs.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name aimed at developers, but slashes in a name are hard to type and search, and evidence of brand pull is limited to GitHub stars and small blog coverage.

outcome_analysis: The company is active in its first year after the Winter 2026 batch. It shipped an open-source Whiteboard beta and a Review app, gained early GitHub attention, and faces strong competition from funded AI code review tools. No exit, shutdown or confirmed round has been found, so the outcome is still open.
